bull.b: Strong operating and free cash flow represent a meaningful turnaround from negative cash generation in 2021–2023. This provides internal funding for product investment, reduces reliance on external capital, and gives DraftKings greater flexibility to support growth while managing its regulated-market cost structure.

Rapid customer acquisition combined with improving acquisition efficiency and higher revenue per unique customer indicates stronger unit economics, not just volume expansion. If sustained, this can broaden the customer base, improve monetization, and support more durable revenue and earnings growth.

The rapid adoption of Predictions adds a growing product category alongside Sportsbook and iGaming, potentially increasing engagement and customer lifetime value. Its expanding volume and limited overlap with the largest prediction operator suggest the product may be incremental rather than substantially cannibalizing existing activity.

bear.b: Debt exceeding three times equity leaves DraftKings more exposed to earnings volatility and reduces financial flexibility. Leverage can constrain the company’s ability to fund aggressive product expansion, absorb weaker operating periods, or allocate cash toward growth while maintaining balance-sheet resilience.

Although revenue has scaled substantially and profitability improved from earlier losses, the return to a net loss and negative operating profit shows that earnings conversion remains inconsistent. This limits confidence that recent cash generation will translate into stable, recurring bottom-line profitability.

The Predictions opportunity requires substantial near-term spending while regulatory questions may delay or limit expansion in certain jurisdictions. That combination could postpone full lifetime-value capture, pressure profitability during the ramp, and increase execution demands before returns on investment become clear.
